v.1: Nun. By the Pen and what they write:
v.2: by your Lord’s blessing, you are not, crazy,
v.3: and yours indeed will be an everlasting reward,
v.4: and indeed you possess a great character.
v.5: You will see and they will see,
v.6: which one of you is crazy.
v.7: Indeed your Lord knows best those who stray from His way, and He knows best those who are guided.
v.8: So do not obey the deniers,
v.9: who are eager that you should be flexible, so that they [too] may be flexible [towards you].
v.10: And do not obey any vile swearer,
v.12: hinderer of all good, sinful transgressor,
v.13: callous and, on top of that, baseborn
v.14: —[who behaves in such a manner only] because he has wealth and children.
v.15: When Our signs are recited to him, he says, ‘Myths of the ancients!’
v.16: Soon We shall brand him on his snout.
v.17: Indeed we have tested them just as We tested the People of the Garden when they vowed they would gather its fruit at dawn,
v.18: and they did not make any exception.
v.19: Then, a visitation from your Lord visited it while they were asleep.
v.20: So, by dawn it was like a harvested field.
v.21: At dawn they called out to one another,
v.22: ‘Get off early to your field if you have to gather [the fruits].’
v.23: So off they went, murmuring to one another:
v.24: ‘Today no needy man shall come to you in it.’
v.25: And they set out at early morning, [considering themselves] able to deprive [the poor of its fruit].
v.26: But when they saw it, they said, ‘We have indeed lost our way!’
v.27: ‘No, it is we who have been deprived!’
v.28: The most upright among them said, ‘Did I not tell you, ‘‘Why do you not glorify [Allah]?’’ ’
v.29: They said, ‘Immaculate is our Lord! We have indeed been wrongdoers!’
v.30: Then they turned to one another, blaming each other.
v.31: They said, ‘Woe to us! Indeed, we have been rebellious.
v.32: Maybe our Lord will give us a better one in its place. Indeed we earnestly beseech our Lord.’
v.33: Such was their punishment; and the punishment of the Hereafter is surely greater, had they known.
v.34: Indeed for the Godwary there will be gardens of bliss near their Lord.
v.35: Shall We treat those who submit [to Us] as [We treat] the guilty?
v.36: What is the matter with you? How do you judge!
v.37: Do you possess a scripture in which you read
v.38: that you shall have in it whatever you choose?
v.39: Do you have a pledge binding on Us until the Day of Resurrection, that you shall indeed have whatever you decide?
v.40: Ask them, which of them will aver [any of] that!
v.41: Do they have any ‘partners’ [that they claim for Allah]? Then let them produce their partners, if they are truthful.
v.42: The day when the catastrophe occurs and they are summoned to prostrate themselves, they will not be able [to do it].
v.43: With a humbled look [in their eyes], they will be overcast by abasement. Certainly, they were summoned to prostrate themselves while they were yet sound.
v.44: So leave Me with those who deny this discourse. We will draw them imperceptibly [into ruin], whence they do not know.
v.45: I will grant them respite, for My devising is indeed sure.
v.46: Do you ask them for a reward, so that they are weighed down with debt?
v.47: Do they possess [access to] the Unseen, so that they write it down?
v.48: So submit patiently to the judgement of your Lord, and do not be like the Man of the Fish who called out as he choked with grief.
v.49: Had it not been for a blessing that came to his rescue from his Lord, he would surely have been cast on the bare shore, being blameworthy.
v.50: So his Lord chose him and made him one of the righteous.
v.51: Indeed the faithless almost devour you with their eyes when they hear this Reminder, and they say, ‘He is indeed crazy.’
v.52: Yet it is just a reminder for all the nations.
